title: Distributed logistics · mission sequence
subtitle: Preposition, disperse, generate and sustain
description: A research visualization of the report's distributed CCA sustainment themes, organized around the support cycle rather than a generic stage-support-return sequence.

citations.locator: Logistics discussion and Figures 11-12; distributed support, prepositioning and constrained logistics

assumptions: The phase structure reflects logistics themes described in the report, while all displayed geography, quantities, routes and timings are editorial illustration.
Timeline seconds are presentation time only and do not represent actual sortie generation, transit, maintenance or replenishment durations.
The visualization does not calculate supply consumption, attrition, throughput, vulnerability or optimal basing.
Support links are conceptual and do not assert real-world access, basing or transportation plans.

phases.title: Preposition
phases.narrative: Introduce forward support resources and replacement capacity positioned before high-risk theater movement becomes more difficult.

phases.title: Disperse
phases.narrative: Show CCA and support activity distributed across multiple operating locations rather than concentrated at a single site.

phases.title: Generate Sorties
phases.narrative: Represent the support network enabling repeated mission generation without assigning real sortie rates or readiness values.

phases.title: Replenish
phases.narrative: Illustrate movement of fuel, munitions, support equipment and replacement capacity as a conceptual logistics relationship.

phases.title: Shift / Rebase
phases.narrative: Show units and support relationships moving among distributed sites as conditions change.

phases.title: Sustain Under Constraint
phases.narrative: Close with constrained sustainment, emphasizing the report's finding that logistics limits can alter force mix and mission support choices.
